From 069c8f5aebe4d5224cf62acc7d4b3486091c658a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Nikola Z. Ivanov" <zlatistiv@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 16:16:43 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net: usb: aqc111: Do not perform PM inside suspend callback

syzbot reports "task hung in rpm_resume"

This is caused by aqc111_suspend calling
the PM variant of its write_cmd routine.

The simplified call trace looks like this:

rpm_suspend()
  usb_suspend_both() - here udev->dev.power.runtime_status == RPM_SUSPENDING
    aqc111_suspend() - called for the usb device interface
      aqc111_write32_cmd()
        usb_autopm_get_interface()
          pm_runtime_resume_and_get()
            rpm_resume() - here we call rpm_resume() on our parent
              rpm_resume() - Here we wait for a status change that will never happen.

At this point we block another task which holds
rtnl_lock and locks up the whole networking stack.

Fix this by replacing the write_cmd calls with their _nopm variants

Reported-by: syzbot+48dc1e8dfc92faf1124c@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=48dc1e8dfc92faf1124c
Fixes: e58ba4544c77 ("net: usb: aqc111: Add support for wake on LAN by MAGIC packet")
Signed-off-by: Nikola Z. Ivanov <zlatistiv@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260313141643.1181386-1-zlatistiv@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/usb/aqc111.c b/drivers/net/usb/aqc111.c
index cbffa9ae1bb6..dd53f413c38f 100644
--- a/drivers/net/usb/aqc111.c
+++ b/drivers/net/usb/aqc111.c
@@ -1395,14 +1395,14 @@ static int aqc111_suspend(struct usb_interface *intf, pm_message_t message)
 		aqc111_write16_cmd_nopm(dev, AQ_ACCESS_MAC,
 					SFR_MEDIUM_STATUS_MODE, 2, &reg16);
 
-		aqc111_write_cmd(dev, AQ_WOL_CFG, 0, 0,
-				 WOL_CFG_SIZE, &wol_cfg);
-		aqc111_write32_cmd(dev, AQ_PHY_OPS, 0, 0,
-				   &aqc111_data->phy_cfg);
+		aqc111_write_cmd_nopm(dev, AQ_WOL_CFG, 0, 0,
+				      WOL_CFG_SIZE, &wol_cfg);
+		aqc111_write32_cmd_nopm(dev, AQ_PHY_OPS, 0, 0,
+					&aqc111_data->phy_cfg);
 	} else {
 		aqc111_data->phy_cfg |= AQ_LOW_POWER;
-		aqc111_write32_cmd(dev, AQ_PHY_OPS, 0, 0,
-				   &aqc111_data->phy_cfg);
+		aqc111_write32_cmd_nopm(dev, AQ_PHY_OPS, 0, 0,
+					&aqc111_data->phy_cfg);
 
 		/* Disable RX path */
 		aqc111_read16_cmd_nopm(dev, AQ_ACCESS_MAC,
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies the file `drivers/net/usb/aqc111.c` to resolve a deadlock (task hung in `rpm_resume`) caused by calling PM-variant write commands inside the suspend callback (`aqc111_suspend`). The fix replaces three specific writes that trigger PM runtime operations with their corresponding `_nopm` variants that bypass PM runtime calls.

### Modifications in Each File

- **File:** `drivers/net/usb/aqc111.c`
  - **Change 1:** In the `if` branch of `aqc111_suspend` (when WoL is configured), replace:
    - `aqc111_write_cmd` with `aqc111_write_cmd_nopm` for the `AQ_WOL_CFG` command.
    - `aqc111_write32_cmd` with `aqc111_write32_cmd_nopm` for the `AQ_PHY_OPS` command.
  - **Change 2:** In the `else` branch (when WoL is not set, entering low power), replace:
    - `aqc111_write32_cmd` with `aqc111_write32_cmd_nopm` for the `AQ_PHY_OPS` command.

### Relationships Between Modifications

All modifications serve the same purpose: prevent PM runtime calls (like `usb_autopm_get_interface` → `pm_runtime_resume_and_get`) from being executed while the USB device is already in the middle of a suspend transition (`RPM_SUSPENDING`). The original calls would cause a nested PM operation that waits indefinitely for a status change, leading to a deadlock and a lockup of the networking stack. The `_nopm` variants avoid this by directly writing the commands without interacting with the PM subsystem. The changes are consistent throughout the suspend path, ensuring no PM-triggering writes occur regardless of the WoL configuration.
